name: Great Hercules Cluster
tagline: M13 — the northern sky's finest globular cluster, ~300,000 stars in a ball 145 light-years wide.
history: Messier 13 is the showpiece globular of the northern hemisphere — a teeming ball several hundred thousand ancient stars strong, hovering in the halo above Hercules. In 1974 the Arecibo radio telescope fired a three-minute binary-encoded message toward M13: humanity's most deliberate hello, aimed at a destination dense enough that any reply takes 50,000 years. At the eyepiece its star lanes resolve into swarming points around a sugared core.
